item.title: Large language model agents in watershed environmental response: a hypothesis-and-theory framework for the cognitive orchestration layer
item.description: Introduction Watershed environmental governance increasingly combines dense sensing infrastructure with institutions whose attention, authority, and coordination capacity remain limited. We develop the cognitive orchestration layer as a theory-building concept for examining how large language model (LLM)-based agents may connect sensing, assessment, decision advice, institutional response, and feedback without displacing domain models or public authority. item.title: Authorization assurance for tool-using LLM agents: a structured review of enforcement semantics and effect-level security evidence
item.description: Abstract Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents exercise authority over protected resources through APIs, tools, credentials, and external services. This structured review asks whether authorization claims are supported at the enforcement and observation boundaries relevant to the claimed effect. item.description: Phygital service research requires evidence of how physical and digital elements jointly produce service outcomes. We develop phygital research fit as alignment among the phenomenon, theory, evidence, research design, and validity and ethical criteria. item.title: MetaNav: Metacognitive Vision-Language Navigation via Reflective Exploration
item.description: Training-free Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents powered by foundation models can follow instructions and explore 3D environments. However, existing approaches rely on greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, leading to inefficient behaviors such as local oscillation and redundant revisiting. item.title: Q-Planner: A Harness System for Quantum Chemistry Agents
item.description: Abstract LLM-based agents for computational chemistry commonly place the model inside an accumulating execution loop, causing context growth proportional to workflow length, unpredictable token costs, and degraded plan reliability at scale. item.description: Agents are increasingly deployed with real autonomy in web application and network penetration testing, where a single out-of-scope action can breach a client’s engagement boundary. item.title: A Governed Computational Architecture for Predictive Process Monitoring with Policy-Constrained Orchestration and Auditable Decision Making
item.description: Abstract Predictive process monitoring enables organizations to anticipate process outcomes from event logs, although deployment in real operational environments remains challenging due to temporal drift, heterogeneous traces, and limited interpretability of deep predictive models. item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
item.description: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. item.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
item.description: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. item.title: LLM Analysis of 150+ Years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals a Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade
item.description: Abstract Migration has been a core topic in German political debate, from postwar expellee displacement to labor migration and recent refugee movements. Large-scale analysis of such political discourse has traditionally required extensive manual annotation, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative. item.title: Coordinating actions and sharing control with a disembodied artificial intelligence: Task-dependent differences from human partners.
item.description: As humans increasingly collaborate with artificial intelligence (AI) systems, understanding how people coordinate their actions with disembodied AI partners is critical for effective human-AI interaction.While corepresentation, the extent to which a partner's actions influence one's own responses has been well studied in human dyads, its role in human-AI interaction remains unclear.Evidence on vicarious agency, the sense of control over a coagent's actions, is similarly mixed for disembodied AI.

item.title: Beyond the Degree: International PhD Graduates’ Employment Journeys Through Self-Regulated Learning and Agency
item.description: Recent research has highlighted how international graduates enact different forms of agency to negotiate their employability. This study extends that line of inquiry by examining how self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies mediate the development of these forms of agency. It utilised a qualitative design, drawing on in-depth interviews with 35 international PhD graduates in Australia.
